Subject: Mutual action plan & regional evaluation: proposed test plan, results, and close timeline

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (Tidal-MAP-v1.docx) that captures the acceptance criteria, evaluation plan, and a proposed two-week close timeline. High-level items:

- Objective: Validate Redwood inference performance at your peak concurrency and confirm multi-region routing & failover behavior for US/EU/APAC.
- Primary metrics: median latency (ms/token), throughput (requests/sec), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and successful concurrent sessions at target QPS.
- Proposed targets for the evaluation run: 95th pct latency < 220ms (US/EU), < 260ms (APAC); TTFT < 350ms under steady-state concurrency; sustained throughput 800–1,000 rps across a 3-node pool.
- Failover checks: simulate regional outage and measure fallback time, request success rate, and any elevation in TTFT.

Can you confirm the acceptance targets above and the two-week close cadence (start on Mon 15 Mar, wrap by Fri 26 Mar)? If those look good I’ll loop in Marcus for the lab runs and Rafael for the routing/failover checklist.

I attached the draft MAP and a placeholder for the test harness inputs. Happy to adjust concurrency/TTFT targets if you have constraints.

Best,
Hannah

Subject: RE: FW: Mutual action plan & regional evaluation: proposed test plan, results, and close timeline

Team — attached are the preliminary run summaries (regional-latency-raw.csv) and a short synthesis below. Tests ran against the Tidal MAP config in a 3-region deployment (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast). Test harness: steady-state 900 rps (60s warmup, 5m steady), spike test at 1,200 rps for 2m, and an APAC control-plane drain at t+9m for 90s to simulate failover.

Preliminary highlights:
- US (us-west): median latency 28ms/token, 95th percentile request latency 180ms, TTFT median 210ms. Sustained throughput stable at 920 rps.
- EU (eu-west): median latency 32ms/token, 95th percentile request latency 205ms, TTFT median 230ms. Sustained throughput stable at 900 rps.
- APAC (ap-southeast): median latency 45ms/token, 95th percentile request latency 245ms, TTFT median 310ms. Sustained throughput stable at 880 rps.
- Spike run (1,200 rps for 2 minutes): brief P95 increases (US 240ms, EU 265ms, APAC 320ms), TTFT for spike windows rose to ~420ms at peak but recovered within 40s after spike end.
- Failover simulation (APAC control-plane drain): average routing fallback observed between 220–340ms measured from client retry to first successful response; error rate during transition ~0.6% (mostly 502/503 transient). All routed requests after fallback succeeded.

Files attached: regional-latency-raw.csv (per-request latencies), failover-screenshot.png (routing-level trace showing the fallback window). I’ll run an extra APAC run with the tighter 240ms 95th window and post results by EOD.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: regional-latency-raw.csv, failover-screenshot.png

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Thompson <claire@tidalai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 12:10:00 -0000
Subject: Results summary & recommended close cadence — Redwood x Tidal eval

Hi Claire and team —

Thanks for flagging the APAC target. Short summary of what we ran and recommended next steps:

What we executed today:
- Steady-state runs across US/EU/APAC at ~900 rps.
- Spike stress test to 1,200 rps for 2 minutes.
- APAC control-plane drain to observe multi-region routing/failover.

Key takeaways (actionable):
- APAC 95th is currently at 245ms (slightly above your tightened 240ms). We’re within 2% of the tighter target; Marcus is re-running an APAC tune with a larger KV cache and an adjusted batching window. Expect updated APAC CSV by EOD.
- Spike behavior is acceptable: transient P95 increases during 2-minute spike with TTFT recovery <45s after spike. We recommend a short client-side retry/backoff of 200ms to mask transient 5xxs during failover windows.
- Failover behavior: routing fallback occurs in ~220–340ms. During that window ~0.6% of requests saw transient 5xx; all requests after fallback completed successfully. We can reduce transient errors by pre-warming nearby model variant and tightening health-check thresholds; that would likely shave ~80–120ms off fallback time in our tests.

Proposed final MAP updates & close timeline:
- Add SLA addendum covering an agreed failover RTO of <=500ms and transient error rate <1.5% during simulated region failover.
- Final APAC run confirm by Fri 12 Mar morning. If APAC P95 <= 240ms, procurement can proceed with DocuSign and we target contract signature by Fri 19 Mar.
- If APAC is in 240–260ms window, we propose a short remediation plan (1 week) post-signature with a commitment to hit 240ms or provide a credit.

Links: full run CSV and a short findings doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cTidalMAP

Claire — happy to jump on a 30-min sync to walk through the traces and the remediation options. Do you want Rafael or Marcus to join procurement calls for the SLA language?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai

Attachment: failover-screenshot.png, regional-latency-raw.csv
